intro: Five long reads people saved with Xtracticle this week — two lab notebooks on code-made motion design, a candid look at how the Claude Code team reviews AI-written code, a one-day life-reset protocol and a Chinese crash course on how AI actually works.

items.author: Florence
items.title: Opus 5.5 Motion Lab: Make Claude Animate Like a Studio
items.summary: A lab notebook of three Opus 5.5 animations, each printed with its original prompt and every follow-up correction, arguing that the unglamorous middle part — the second and third prompt — is where studio-quality motion comes from.

items.author: DAN KOE
items.title: How to fix your entire life in 1 day
items.summary: Dan Koe argues that resolutions fail because people change their actions instead of their identity, and closes with a day-long protocol for working out what you actually want before setting any goal.

items.author: Addy Osmani
items.title: How the Claude Code team does code review
items.summary: Addy Osmani explains how the Claude Code team kept reviewing code while merge volume doubled: automated review runs before a human looks, human attention is saved for design-level questions, and reverting became fast and cheap.

items.author: 龙井longjing
items.title: 2小时从零看懂 AI：一篇文章建立AI认知体系（8000元企业内训同款）
items.summary: A two-hour corporate AI training course rewritten as one long article: what large models are, how to write prompts, what agents are and how to build a first one, aimed at readers starting from zero.

items.author: rari🈀
items.title: Motion Engineering: Build a Video Studio Around Opus 5.5
items.summary: Rari describes a five-layer pipeline for making videos with Opus 5.5 — the model writes a frame function, a renderer draws it, and a review loop decides what ships — so the next clip can be produced without rebuilding the whole setup.
